REPRODUCER (scratch/s519a/pr/pt5.pl):
    my @s = CORE::stat("i/do/not/exist"); print scalar(@s), "\n";      # 0 both
    sub pop_ { return undef unless @_; "obj" }
    print defined(pop_(CORE::stat("i/do/not/exist"))) ? "def\n" : "undef\n";
perl 5.40.3: `0` `undef`.  PCL: `0` `def` -- the empty list a failed stat returns becomes ONE argument when it is a call argument (the list-assignment slot is right).
WHERE IT BITES: core File::stat 1.14 `stat` is `my $st = populate(CORE::stat $arg); return $st if defined $st;` and populate starts `return undef unless @_` -- so File::stat::stat on a missing path returns a File::stat object, and Path::Tiny `->stat` / `->lstat` (`File::stat::stat(...) || $self->_throw(...)`) never throw: Path-Tiny t/filesystem.t rows 15-16 (`ok exception { path($file)->stat }`).
Probe also plain `stat` / `lstat` in an argument slot, and a failed `localtime`-like list builtin, before fixing (the shared builtin-in-a-list-slot path, rule 11).
